main.description: Get the private-tier replies to a post that the requester is authorized to read, oldest first, each as a thread node with its own replies expanded `depth` levels below it. The post may be a private-tier post (tools.kryphocron.feed.postPrivate) or a public app.bsky.feed.post. A private post is read for the requester as getPosts reads it; a private post the requester may not read and one that does not exist give the same answer, {replies: []}. A public post is not read: only its private replies are listed, and nothing about the public post is returned. When the thread's root, as the post's record claims it, is a private post the requester may read, the replies its threadgate hides are left out, except for the requester's own. At most 200 nodes; at most 50 replies a node below the first level; deeper levels are reached by calling getReplies on a node. Requires auth by a ready community member. Audiences this AppView resolves: `list` (the audience record's members); `followers` (followers of the audience's owner who are ready members of this AppView, by the follow records it has indexed, which reflect a new follow or an unfollow within about a minute); `everyone` (every ready member of this AppView, not the network); and `nobody`. `following`: the accounts the audience's owner follows that are ready members of this AppView, by the follow records it has indexed, once it has compared them with the owner's repository. Until then, and always for an owner that follows more than 50 000 accounts, a `following` audience is read by its owner alone, and replies under it by their authors alone. An unfollow stops reads within about a minute. A `following` post appears in a reader's timeline only when the reader also follows its owner. When neither the owner nor a replier is a ready member, and this AppView is not indexing public records, the owner's follow of the replier is not indexed, so that reply is read by its author alone. Any other mode is served to its author only. A block record or a private block between the reader and the author, or the audience's owner, in either direction, keeps the reader out; a block through a list does not. A reply is read by the readers of its thread root's current audience, or, in a private branch under a public post, of its branch root's current audience. It is served only when all of these hold: its root (or branch root) is stored, names an audience of its own author, and is visible; the reply names an audience of that author; its author, and the author of every post above it in its chain other than the root's author, may write under the root's current audience now, by the PDS's rule for that mode, and there is no block either way between them and the root's author; its chain of parents, through stored private posts agreeing on its root, reaches a post by the root's author (or the branch root) within 16 posts (this AppView's `max_chain`), each visible to the reader. The root author's own replies in a thread are not walked, and are read by the root's audience whatever audience they name. Replies deeper than the bound, or below someone who no longer stands under the current audience, are read only by their authors, except the root author's own thread replies. A post is never served to a reader where either has blocked the other. Its author always reads it, unless moderation hides it, even when the thread's owner has blocked the author or removed them from the audience. `audience` on the view is the governing audience.

uri.description: The post whose replies to list: a private-tier post or a public app.bsky.feed.post.

limit.description: How many direct replies a page holds.

cursor.description: Opaque, sealed pagination cursor from a previous response to the same requester for the same uri. Any other cursor is rejected with InvalidRequest.

depth.description: How many levels of replies to include below each direct reply; 0 includes none.

cursor.description: Present whenever more candidates remain. A page reads at most twice its `limit` in candidates. It can be short or empty and still carry a cursor; keep paging while a cursor is present. Absent at the end, and also, exceptionally, when the last examined position is too long to seal (a reply whose author's did:web is several hundred characters), where the list ends early.

errors.name: NotEnrolled
errors.description: The caller is not a community member of this AppView.

errors.name: NotReady
errors.description: The caller's account indexing is still in progress.
